title: Over-hedged a design question by presenting three options instead of doing the obvious fix
details:
- **What happened:** Asked why the FormatJS parser ships at runtime and whether there is an alternative, the model had already verified a working fix (aliasing to the no-parser entry) but presented three options and asked the user to choose, treating an earlier passing remark ("driven by formatjs") as a constraint.
- **What the user said:** "we don't have to treat something I said in passing as some kind of contract. if there are better options we should use them? I don't need you to hedge in every direction - why wouldn't we just use the no-parser entry you used to test?"
- **Repro:** Design discussion in a greenfield repo; model measures a fix that works, then replies with an options list and "Which way do you want to go?" instead of applying it.
